verdict.rationale: Base44's own docs describe connecting an app to GitHub so code written locally or in Base44 stays in sync with each other. That is first-party, two-way sync for version control and local development. The evidence is only short summary lines, though. Missing for 10: details on repo ownership and setup (e.g., the user's own account or org repo), how conflicts or merges are handled, and independent or hands-on confirmation that two-way sync works in practice.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync my project to my own GitHub repository and keep changes flowing both ways

citations.quote: Connect your app to GitHub to write code in your local development environment or in Base44 and keep them in sync with each other.
Connect your Base44 app to GitHub for version control, local development, and collaboration.
